newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 7.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 7.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
DUESSELDORF - Media agency Optimedia Gesellschaft fuer Media Services mbH says its has named Norbert Anderman as a new managing director along side Christian Cuntz and Horst Plueger.
(Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Automaker Nissan Motor Deutschland has reorganised its marketing budget, leaving current account holder HF&P to battle with TBWA of Duesseldorf and Hamburg-based Zum goldenen Hirschen over representation rights to the multimillion-mark account. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Sportwear manufacturer Reebok International and advertisisng agency Leo Burnett of Chicago have after four years ended their cooperation. Both companies say the separation was mutually agreed upon. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - The Association of Private Broadcasting and Telecommunications (VPRT) has called on telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom AG to make public its strategy for the future use of its cable television network before an industry summit on May 20. (Reuter)
MUNICH - The top games in the soccer world championships will continue to be shown on "free television" in Germany, and not on a pay-per-view basis. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)
FRANKFURT - The EU commission is examining whether the fee-financing of German television stations Phoenix and Kinderkanal comply with European fair competition laws.
(Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)

MUNICH - Media company ProSieben Media AG says it has sold its 50 percent share in Navigo Multimedia Produktions - GmbH & Co to publishing group Burda. The company says there was too little "synergy" between the television and CD-Rom businesses.
(Reuter)

LUDWIGSHAFEN - The first digital television licences have been issued in Germany, clearing the way for a summer trial run, media officials in the western state of Rhineland-Palatinate say. Digital service DF1, pay television channel Premiere and programming package MultiThematiques received broadcasting permits and cable slots from the state private broadcasting authority (LPR) for a pilot digital television service.
(Reuter)

KRONBERG - Turks living in Germany have emerged as a key target group for television advertisers, media marketing company IP Deutschland says. Ninety-seven percent of Turkish Germans watch television several times a week, compared with 91 percent of ethnic Germans, the company says. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

ZURICH - Nestle SA chairman Helmut Maucher forecasts that the world's biggest food company will post double-digit gains in sales and profits in 1997 after a weak Swiss franc helped to boost first quarter turnover by 18.7 percent. (Reuter)

STUTTGART - Computer company IBM is moving from being primarily a computer and programming manufacturer to a service provider, the company's Central European director Willi Berchtold says. Berchtold says the service business as become IBM's "growth engine", expanding at a 25 percent highter rate than the market.
(Reuter)

DORTMUND - Beer company Dortmunder Actien-Braurei AG (DAB) says it reported no growth in profits in fiscal year 1996. DAB chairman Wolfgang Burghard says the generally weak food and beverage business has hurt sales. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Beverage group Eckes AG says it posted higher turnover and profits for 1996, despite corporate restructuring, higher raw materials costs and stronger competition in the industry. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

HAMBURG - The chief executive of oil company RWE-DEA, Dieter Draeger, will also begin as chief of DEA Mineraloel AG in 1998. Beginning in early 1998, the finance director of RWE-DEA, Sigurd Beyer, will serve on the board of DEA Mineraloel. (Reuter)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
